senses.gloss: (also, figuratively) A shop that offers a wide variety of goods for sale; a department store; (with a descriptive word) a shop specializing in particular goods.
A Turkish city, and the largest European city by population, which was the last capital of the Ottoman Empire and the Byzantine Empire (Eastern Roman Empire).
Specifically, a small amount of time.
To a small extent or degree.
To a limited extent or degree; not completely.
A small amount; a little bit.
Having a relatively high voltage.
Having a bad reputation; disreputable; notorious; unpleasant or evil; widely known, especially for something scornful.
Easily understood or appreciated.
Arousing or holding the attention or interest of someone.
To ease (a person, person's thoughts etc.) from mental distress; to stop (someone) feeling anxious or worried, to alleviate the distress of.
Nonsense; bullshit.
To place (any one cognition) under another as belonging to it; to include or contain something else.
overwhelm
To take a photograph (of).
To serve as a warning or omen of.

A piece of information describing, or an account of certain events given or presented to someone, with the most common adpositions being by (referring to creator of the report) and on (referring to the subject).
An appraisal or evaluation.
A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.
(collective) A group of donkeys.
A cattle drive or the herd being driven by it; thus, a number of cattle driven to market or new pastures.
A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.
A number of birds together in a group, such as those gathered together for the purpose of migration.
A large number of insects, especially when in motion or (for bees) migrating to a new colony.
A group, especially a large group, and especially a group of attractive girls or women.
wire fastener used to secure stacks of paper
A device which binds together sheets of paper by driving a thin metal staple through the sheets and simultaneously folding over the ends of the staple against the back surface of the paper.
(Christianity) A title given to Jesus of Nazareth, seen as the fulfiller of the messianic prophecy.
The act of sending an accused person back into custody whilst awaiting trial.
One who is not intimately familiar with a given subject or activity.
after everything else; finally
Indicating the last item.
An attainment or arrival at the highest pitch of glory, power, etc.
A collection of tools; a toolkit.
(dated, dialectal) A thicket; a small wood or grove.
A small forest.
Worthy of pity.
Having a bad reputation; disreputable; notorious; unpleasant or evil; widely known, especially for something scornful.
Showing or characterized by a contemptible lack of moral standards.
A person who formally opposes the current political structure, the political group in power, the policies of the political group in power, or current laws.
Of or pertaining to heresy or heretics.
A person who likes or tends to express a contradicting viewpoint, especially from one held by a majority of people, usually because of nonconformity or spite. [from mid 20th c.]
Someone who does not conform to accepted beliefs, customs or practices. [from 17th c.]
Someone who dissents (disagrees), especially from an established church.
Believing without question; having absolute loyalty.
Not negotiable; not subject to negotiation.
A place for conducting trading.
(education) A merit-based scholarship.
(education) A scholarship granted to a student. [from Template:SAFESUBST: c.]
Introducing an explanation
Suave; sophisticated.
Characterised by or exhibiting elegance; having grace, refinement, or tasteful simplicity.
Well-mannered, civilized.
Made smooth or shiny by polishing.
Marked by refinement in taste and manners.
Characterised by careful and conscious thought.
Showing regard or thought for others; especially, displaying good manners or etiquette.
Having good manners; polite, courteous, and socially correct; conforming to standards of good behaviour.
The act of oppressing, or the state of being oppressed.
A cruel act.
The act of persecuting, especially a specific group of people; an instance of persecution.
A government in which a single ruler (a tyrant) has absolute power, or this system of government; especially, one that acts cruelly and unjustly.
(countable) An act of great injustice or unfairness; a sinful or wicked act; an unconscionable deed.
At a slow pace.
To augment or make something greater.
To increase; to make larger or supplement.
A complete domicile occupying only part of a building, especially one for rent; a flat.
A malfunction.
Termination of the ability of an item to perform its required function; breakdown.

Faulty functioning.
A quality of being inadequate; a disadvantage, a fault.
The seed within the drupe of a small deciduous tree in family Rosaceae, Prunus amygdalus, considered a culinary nut.
In a due, fit, or becoming manner; as it ought to be; suitably; properly.
Something put forth, bid, proffered or tendered.
gerund of offer
Highly accurate or definitive; treated or worthy of treatment as a scholarly authority.
A regular polyhedron having six identical square faces.
(geometry) Used in the names of units of volume formed by multiplying a unit of length by itself twice.
plural of jean
A textile often made of cotton with a distinct diagonal pattern.
Movable rails which can be used to switch a train from one railway track to another.
place where railways meet
A tool used for cutting thin material, consisting of two crossing blades attached at a pivot point in such a way that the blades slide across each other when the handles are closed.
A structure made up of one or more triangular units made from straight beams of wood or metal, which is used to support a structure as in a roof or bridge.

A cutting tool used to remove parts of stone, wood or metal by pushing or pounding the back when the sharp edge is against the material. It consists of a slim, oblong block of metal with a sharp wedge or bevel formed on one end and sometimes a handle at the other end; there are hand tool versions (the original type) and versions as bits for power tools.
(rail transport) A switch on a railway used to move a train from one track to another.
The manipulation of railway rolling stock into different combinations or onto different tracks.
Of a car, running on both fuel (gasoline or diesel) and electricity (battery or energy from the sun).
(dated, derogatory, offensive, ethnic slur) A person of mixed racial parentage or ancestry, especially one of mixed white and American Indian parentage (metis, métis, Metis, Métis; mestizo).
mongrel
someone of mixed kind
A coniferous tree, of genus Larix, having deciduous leaves in fascicles.
Of mixed heritage
person of mixed ancestry
To exercise sovereign power, to rule as a monarch.
To keep away from; to keep clear of; to stay away from.
(ambitransitive) To avoid (something) by moving suddenly out of the way.
To avoid an obstacle etc, by constructing or using a bypass.
To avoid, especially persistently; ostracize.
(transitive, figuratively) To avoid addressing (questions, criticism, etc.).
(transitive) to avoid or get around something; to bypass
To turn aside or deviate to avoid impact.
(transitive) To evade or escape from (someone or something), especially by using cunning or skill.
The act of one who vomits, or the matter that is vomited.
Of or like a bastard (bad person).
A formal dance.
A formal ball held at a high school or college on special occasions; e.g., near the end of the academic year.
A strip of cloth worn around the neck and tied in the front.
The origin, start, or point at which something comes into being.

A small long and narrow boat, propelled by one or more people (depending on the size of canoe), using single-bladed paddles. The paddlers face in the direction of travel, in either a seated position, or kneeling on the bottom of the boat. Canoes are open on top, and pointed at both ends.
The study of the effects of geography (especially economic geography) on international politics.
A state of the United States.
The characteristic of being humble; humbleness in character and behavior.
A person who worships, especially at a place of assembly for religious services.
Uncomfortably restricted in size or space, or financially.
(figurative) Inactivity; a freezing, or state of motionlessness.
(UK, Irish, Commonwealth) A line of motor vehicles causing or the result of traffic congestion or a traffic jam.
A hanging seat that can swing back and forth, in a children's playground, for acrobats in a circus, or on a porch for relaxing.

An organ in most mammals during gestation that supplies food and oxygen to the foetus and passes back waste. It is on the wall of the uterus and links to the foetus through the umbilical cord. It is expelled after birth.
The placenta and other material expelled via the birth canal following childbirth or parturition in mammals.
weight for training muscles
A form of exercise in which weights are lifted.
A wide steel bar with premeasured weights counterpoised at either end, with the central span open for the hands of the weightlifter.
A weight training implement consisting of a short bar with weight counterpoised on each end.
Of or relating to the New Stone Age.
Full of rancor; bitter; unforgiving.

A geographic region and de-facto independent but largely unrecognized country on the coast of the Black Sea and the south-western flank of the Caucasus on the border of Europe and Asia, which considers itself an independent state called the Republic of Abkhazia; considered part of Georgia's territory by the Georgian government and the vast majority of the international community.
Without scruples; immoral.
Not conscionable; unscrupulous and lacking principles or conscience.
Lacking a conscience; unscrupulous or ruthless.
A machine for creating bales, e.g., of hay or cotton.
A blow, especially one given with the open hand, or with something broad and flat.
The state or quality of being white (all senses).
A rank directly below class.
That which is believed; accepted doctrine, especially religious doctrine; a particular set of beliefs; any summary of principles or opinions professed or adhered to.
A statement of a belief or a summary statement of a whole belief system; also (metonymically) the belief or belief system itself.
A port town, the administrative center of the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, in extreme northeastern Russia.
In a meaningless manner; nonsensically.
Opposition to communism.
An Ashkenazi Jew.
A wingback chair.
A piece of nonfiction writing such as a story, report, opinion piece, or entry in a newspaper, magazine, journal, encyclopedia, etc.
An attractive man, especially one who is muscular.
A large, lush, undeveloped, humid forest, especially in a tropical region, thick with vegetation and wildlife; a tropical rainforest.
A person or thing that interprets the meaning of something for another
The sport of hunting by using trained birds of prey, especially falcons and hawks.
Of or pertaining to the region and culture of Etruria, a pre-Roman civilization in Italy.
An autonomous territorial unit of Moldova.
Any of several flowering plants, of the genus Gladiolus, having sword-shaped leaves and showy flowers on spikes; gladiola.

A syrupy sweet liquid obtained as a by-product in the manufacture of soap from animal or vegetable oils and fats; it is used as an antifreeze, a plasticizer, and a food sweetener and in the manufacture of dynamite, cosmetics etc.
Synonym of glycerol
A clamour, a commotion; a fuss or uproar.
room used for urination and defecation — see also bathroom, men's room, ladies' room, outhouse, portable toilet, latrine, shitter, water closet
Ellipsis of public convenience (“a public lavatory”).
Any facility or device used for urination or defecation, whether toilet, lavatory, or outhouse.
A port city, a municipal and regional administrative centre of Kherson raion, Kherson oblast, Ukraine, located on the Dnieper/Dnipro.
(pathology) A too low level of blood glucose.
A hold or way of holding, particularly with the hand.
The handle of a sword, consisting of grip, guard, and pommel, designed to facilitate use of the blade and afford protection to the hand.
A pin, or handle, of the snath (shaft) of a scythe.
A projection that one may hold onto for support, e.g. in mountain climbing.
A dark, extremely viscous material still remaining after distilling crude oil or natural tar.
deliberately kill

To kill in considerable numbers where little or no resistance can be made, with indiscriminate violence, without necessity, and contrary to civilized norms. (Often limited to the killing of human beings.)
To massacre people in large numbers.
To make or become hard and stony by impregnating with calcium salts.
A person to whom a debt is owed.
To make strong or stronger; to add strength to; to increase the strength of; to fortify.
To strengthen, especially by addition or augmentation.
To impart vigor, strength, or vitality to.
Any of various wingless hexapods, of the subclass Collembola, with spring-like legs. [from 18th c.]
Getting worse.
(transitive) To make defamatory statements about; to slander or traduce.

The fundamental force of attraction which exists between all matter in the universe that tends to draw bodies towards each other, due to matter causing the curvature of spacetime. It is the weakest of the four fundamental interactions, and possesses a gauge boson known as the graviton.

(constellation) A small constellation of the southern sky, said to resemble a goldfish or swordfish. It lies between the constellations Pictor and Reticulum, and is notable for containing most of the Large Magellanic Cloud.
To bend or turn gradually from a given direction.
rigid tube
The record of a single event or item.
(business, management) The tangible end product; that which will be delivered.
To react, using fermentation; especially to produce alcohol by aging or by allowing yeast to act on sugars; to brew.
Tending, or causing, to recede from the center.
device for separation of substances
An approval, by an authority, generally one that makes something valid.

The monomer constituting DNA or RNA biopolymer molecules. Each nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous heterocyclic base (or nucleobase), which can be either a double-ringed purine or a single-ringed pyrimidine; a five-carbon pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA or ribose in RNA); and a phosphate group.
Lacking recent experience, out of practice, especially with respect to a skill or activity.
Speaking openly and honestly, neglecting privacy and consequences.
To restore to health.
The state of being a serf.
A city and port, the capital of the province of Syracuse, Sicily, Italy.
Reverence and devotion to God.
To leave in a hurry; to go away.
to flee, often secretly
Inflexible and unwilling to negotiate or make concessions.
Unwilling to compromise or moderate a position; unreasonable.
On, spanning or crossing, or from the other side of the Atlantic Ocean.
beyond or on the other side of an ocean
A garment worn over the torso, with or without sleeves, and of various lengths reaching from the hips to the ankles.
A slit in the seam of a garment.
Without effort.

The quality of being patient.
A small, common warbler, of species Phylloscopus collybita, with yellowish-green plumage that breeds throughout northern and temperate Europe and Asia.

A device to which a bundle of natural fibres (often wool, flax, or cotton) is attached for temporary storage, before being drawn off gradually to spin thread. A traditional distaff is a staff with flax fibres tied loosely to it (as indicated by the etymology of the word), but modern distaffs are often made of cords weighted with beads, and attached to the wrist.
A blow, especially one given with the open hand, or with something broad and flat.
(uncountable) A form of physical punishment in which a beating is applied to the buttocks.
